title: HIPAA readiness seller briefing and FAQ
content:
Purpose:
This brief is a compact, seller-facing reference to confidently engage healthcare buyers about Redwood Inference’s HIPAA readiness, related controls (SOC2 / ISO27001 alignment), data handling practices, and standardized audit-log language. Intended for AEs, SEs, and solution engineering during discovery and procurement.

Audience and usage notes:
- Primary: Enterprise AEs and SEs responding to healthcare and life-sciences opportunities (mid-market and up).
- Secondary: CSMs preparing handoff, and marketing for one-pagers.
- Use: live demos, RFP responses, security questionnaires, presales calls, and BAA negotiations.

Three core messaging pillars (elevator-friendly):
1) Data separation + choice: customers can run on Hosted with strong isolation, on Dedicated capacity for committed pools, or in Private (VPC / on-prem) when regulatory boundaries demand it. We provide the same API and rollout primitives across modes so integrations stay consistent.
2) Control + visibility: end-to-end encryption, fine-grained IAM, customer-managed KMS options, and detailed audit-logs with immutable trails. We surface token-level cost and latency but also record access events useful for audits.
3) Operational assurance: SOC2 controls and ISO-aligned practices form our baseline; for PHI workloads we require a BAA paired with either Dedicated or Private deployments plus documented operational runbooks.

High-level technical posture (what to mention in calls):
- Encryption: TLS1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest by default. Customers may bring keys (KMS/HSM) in Private and Dedicated setups.
- Multitenancy and isolation: hosted tenancy is strongly partitioned; sensitive regulated workloads are recommended for Dedicated or Private depending on risk appetite.
- Logging & auditability: request-level logs, authentication events, and admin actions are retained with configurable retention and export to customer SIEM. Audit logs are tamper-evident and can be exported via S3 or pushed to customer endpoints.
- Data minimization and retention: configurable token and prompt retention policies; configurable automatic redaction for sensitive fields at ingestion.
- Model behavior and data exposure: transient KV caches; no training on customer interaction data without explicit opt-in and contract language.

BAA and deployment guidance (seller checklist):
- For PHI (HIPAA) customers: trigger BAA conversation early. BAAs are supported only when customer uses Dedicated or Private deployments because we require clearer data boundaries and KMS options.
- Document the expected data flows in the presales packet: where PHI enters, how it moves, where it is stored (if at all), and which systems can access it.
- Offer a short architecture diagram (one-page) mapping customer network to Redwood endpoints; call out encryption, KMS, and audit export path.

Sample audit-log language (short / quick answer):
- Short: "We provide immutable audit logs covering API requests, authentication/authorization events, and admin changes. Logs can be retained per customer policy and exported to your SIEM. We support tamper-evident storage and customer-managed key encryption for exported artifacts."

Sample audit-log language (detailed, for security questionnaires or RFPs):
- Detailed: "Redwood Inference generates detailed audit logs for all customer-facing operations, including: API request metadata (timestamp, operation, model, route, request/response size metrics), authentication and authorization events (actor, role, IP, outcome), and platform administrative actions (deployments, config changes, key rotations). Logs are written to append-only storage and signed with platform keys to provide tamper-evidence. Customers can configure retention policies and choose export destinations (S3, GCS, syslog, or direct SIEM ingestion). For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed encryption (KMS/HSM) for both runtime and exported logs."

Competitive differentiators to highlight (talking points):
- Unified API across deployment modes — avoids multiple integrations when customers move from evaluation to dedicated/private production.
- Transparent audit language prepared for RFPs: we provide both short-form and high-detail snippets ready to paste, reducing procurement friction.
- Operational SLAs tied to Dedicated capacity and documented runbooks for incident response — useful for regulated customers who need playbooks during audits.

Common seller objections and rebuttals: 
- "We can’t send PHI to third-party hosted endpoints." -> "We support Dedicated and Private deployments that satisfy boundary and contractual requirements for PHI; we will sign a BAA and can arrange customer-managed KMS and network egress rules so PHI never leaves your controlled perimeter if required."
- "How do I prove logs are tamper-evident?" -> "We use append-only storage and cryptographic signing for log bundles; we can provide examples of signed exports and work with your auditors or third-party assessors to validate log integrity."
- "Do you train models on our data?" -> "No training on customer content without an explicit, contract-level opt-in. Redactions and retention policies are configurable to minimize exposure."

Presales scripts (concise):
- Discovery: "Can you confirm whether the workload contains PHI/PII and whether you plan to sign a BAA? That informs whether we should propose Hosted with strict controls or move directly to Dedicated/Private."
- Security call opener: "We align to SOC2 controls and practice ISO-aligned processes; for PHI we pair a signed BAA with Dedicated or Private deployments and provide an architecture diagram and audit-log export for your SIEM."

One-page technical appendix (bulleted talking points):
- SOC2: We maintain SOC2 Type II reports; we can provide custom bridge letters for limited review periods.
- ISO27001: We follow a subset of ISO-aligned processes for asset classification and risk management; customers requiring full certification can request detailed control mappings.
- HIPAA: BAA required + Dedicated/Private recommended. Documented data flows + retention and redaction settings.
- Logging: Event types (API, auth, admin), retention controls, export endpoints, tamper-evidence, optional encryption by customer.

FAQ (ready lines):
Q: "Do you export PHI to model providers?"
A: "No — we do not send customer PHI to external model providers. For hosted models we operate the inference stack; model weights are not retrained on customer prompts unless explicitly contracted."

Q: "What rolling window for logs do you keep by default?"
A: "Default retention for hosted customers is 90 days; Dedicated customers can configure longer retention and on-prem customers manage retention themselves. We can also deliver archival exports for audit purposes."

Q: "How quickly can I get a signed BAA?"
A: "Standard BAA turnaround is 2–4 weeks depending on redlines and legal review; involve your procurement early and we’ll route to enterprise legal. For urgent pilots we can provide a conditional scoping addendum while legal finalizes the BAA."

Open questions / follow-ups for product & security teams (for internal use):
- Finalize standardized audit-log schema example (CSV + JSON sample) for export by end of Q1 2026.
- Define default redaction rules and an admin UI for configuring regex-based redactions in hosted mode.
- Clarify the exact SOC2 scope and provide a concise control mapping doc for HIPAA-relevant controls (e.g., access control, audit logging, change management).

Attachments to produce for the sales kit (action items):
1) 1-page HIPAA presales diagram (network + data flows) — to be kept in the shared presales slide deck.
2) Paste-ready audit-log snippets (short + detailed) — load into Sales playbook snippets.
3) BAA template (legal) and BAA checklist for SEs.
4) Exportable sample log bundle (signed) demonstrating tamper-evidence.

Notes on tone and redlines:
- Keep public-facing claims conservative: avoid "HIPAA certified" phrasing (use "HIPAA-ready with BAA + Dedicated/Private deployments").
- When in doubt, escalate to Security for exact control language.

Bottom line for sellers to carry:
We can support PHI workloads — but it requires the right deployment and contract (BAA). Emphasize deployment choice, audit logs/exportability, encryption options, and that we won’t train on customer data without consent. Use the short and detailed audit-log snippets when responding to questionnaires to reduce friction.
